prerequisites: Passing the basic Mathematics and Physics exams scheduled in the first two years of the degree course is strongly recommended.
Fundamental knowledge of basic circuit theory and Electrical Engineering is also important.

learning_outcomes.text: Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic wave propagation, transmission line theory, and basic antenna parameters.
Solving simple propagation problems and evaluating operational parameters of transmission lines (impedance matching).
Ability to choose between lumped-circuit and distributed-parameter models for simple high-frequency problems.
Clear presentation of concepts using appropriate scientific and technical terminology.
Ability to consult introductory technical textbooks and attend advanced courses in electronic and biomedical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Vector calculus review: gradient, divergence, curl, and their physical meaning
Maxwell's equations in time and frequency domains
Maxwell's equations in matter, constitutive relations, and physical realizability conditions
Fundamental theorems of electromagnetics: Poynting theorem, reciprocity, equivalence, and duality
Propagation in plasmas: cold collisionless plasma model and ionospheric propagation; wave packet, phase and group velocities
Distributed-parameter circuit model and TEM modes
Transmission line equations in time and frequency domains
Reflection coefficient, standing wave ratio, and impedance transformation formulas
Impedance matching techniques: matched lines, quarter-wave transformer, and single-stub tuning
Retarded electrodynamic potentials and electromagnetic radiation in free space
Fundamental parameters of transmitting antennas: effective length, radiation vector, directivity, gain, and effective area
Main lobe characterization for directive antennas and basic principles of receiving antennas
teaching_methods: Classroom lectures supported by slides and multimedia material
assessment_rules: The exam consists of an oral examination aimed at assessing the comprehension of course contents. The final grade is expressed on a 30-point scale, with a minimum passing grade of 18/30. Honors (cum laude) are awarded for outstanding preparation and comprehensive mastery of the subject.
bibliography: D. J. Griffiths, "Introduction to Electrodynamics", Cambridge University Press.
J. D. Jackson, "Classical Electrodynamics", John Wiley & Sons.
Lecture notes, slides, and supplementary learning materials provided by the instructor on the University e-learning platform (Handy).
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Elettronica E Biomedica (Electronics And Biomedical Engineering), classe L-8 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria dell'informazione
